titles: Sakurajima stays at JMA alert Level 3
Sakurajima's 2 km zone stays shut in Kagoshima
Sakurajima erupts 6 times, ash keeps rising
Sakurajima's gas output tops 2,100 tons daily

facts.fact: Sakurajima's Minami-dake summit crater erupted at 2:25pm JST on 14 Sept; JMA's ashfall forecast (issued 2:46pm) said the resulting plume rose 2,500 m above the crater rim.
JMA's forecast for the 14 Sept eruption said ash drifted north and predicted 'moderately heavy' (やや多量) ashfall in Kagoshima city by 8:00pm that evening.
The same 14 Sept forecast said lighter ashfall was expected as far as Asagiri Town in neighboring Kumamoto Prefecture.
JMA's 14 Sept 16:00 activity bulletin, covering 11-14 Sept, recorded 6 eruptions at Sakurajima's Minami-dake summit crater in that span, with ash reaching a maximum 2,500 m above the crater rim.
Ballistic volcanic rocks from those 11-14 Sept eruptions were thrown as far as roughly 600 m from the Minami-dake summit crater.
[Background, >72h old] On 11 Sept, JMA logged 9 volcanic earthquakes at Sakurajima with zero explosions that day.
[Background, borderline >72h] On 12 Sept, JMA logged 7 volcanic earthquakes at Sakurajima with zero explosions.
On 13 Sept, JMA logged 6 volcanic earthquakes at Sakurajima with zero explosions.
By 3:00pm on 14 Sept, JMA had logged 3 volcanic earthquakes that day, with zero explosions across the full 11-14 Sept window.

JMA's 14 Sept bulletin states sulfur dioxide (volcanic gas) discharge remains 'generally abundant' and that magma continues accumulating deep beneath the Aira Caldera, so eruptive activity is expected to continue.
JMA's next scheduled Sakurajima activity bulletin is due 18 Sept at 16:00 JST.

On 13 Sept, Sakurajima produced an ash plume of 2,400 m; JMA's forecast that day had ash drifting northwest toward Kagoshima city's Yoshino area, with 'moderately heavy' ashfall expected in Kagoshima city by 11:00pm and lighter fall reaching as far as Akune city.
facts.source_name: MBC (Minami Nippon Broadcasting) via docomo topics

facts.fact: Sakurajima remains at Japan's Volcanic Alert Level 3 (entry restriction/入山規制) — a status JMA and Kagoshima City documentation date to 27 July 2022 and which is still in force as of 14 Sept 2026.

A 2 km no-entry restricted zone around the Minami-dake and Showa craters remains in force under Article 63 of Japan's Disaster Countermeasures Basic Law, citing danger from large ballistic rocks and pyroclastic flows.
The Tokyo VAAC's most recent Sakurajima ash advisory (No. 2026/192) was issued at 05:39 UTC (14:39 JST) on 14 Sept, part of a rapid run of advisories (2026/189 through 2026/192) issued 13-14 Sept.
[Background, >72h old] On 8 Sept, an eruption at Minami-dake produced an ash plume of 1,300 m above the crater rim.
facts.source_name: JMA volcanic activity data (via web search summary)

facts.fact: [Background, >72h old] A JMA field survey on 10 Sept measured Sakurajima's sulfur dioxide emission rate at 2,100 tonnes per day.
facts.source_name: JMA volcanic activity data (via web search summary)

facts.fact: [Background, >72h old] Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program / VolcanoDiscovery reporting on Aira (Sakurajima) covering 6-12 Aug 2026 recorded ongoing eruptive activity since early August, ash plumes up to 2.2 km, ballistics to 600 m, and Alert Level 3 maintained.

[Background, >72h old, different event — May 2026] Sakurajima produced a small pyroclastic flow (~600 m, southeast) confirmed 8 May 2026, its first in roughly eight years, alongside episodes of mountain-body (edifice) inflation feeding the same magma-accumulation pattern JMA cites for the current unrest.

[Background, standing planning figure, undated] Kagoshima City's official hazard guidance says ash from a major Sakurajima eruption could reach depths of '1 m or more' within a 20 km radius, and pyroclastic flows can travel at over 100 km/h.

unknowns: No on-record quote from a named individual official (a JMA spokesperson, the Fukuoka District Meteorological Observatory, Kagoshima's mayor, or the Kagoshima governor) was found in the sources checked for the 10-14 Sept 2026 window — only unattributed agency bulletin text ('JMA says...') was available, so no quotes are reported.

No verified flight-cancellation count for Kagoshima Airport specific to 10-14 Sept 2026 was found; all flight-cancellation figures located (30 flights, Nov 2025; ~34 flights across Kagoshima/Kumamoto/Miyazaki, Nov 2025; 4 flights, May 2025) are from unrelated, older eruptions and must not be read as this week's numbers.
JMA has not stated whether it is considering raising the Alert Level above 3, nor has it announced any change to the standing 2 km restricted zone during this window.
No quantified ashfall depth (mm) for Kagoshima city on 13-14 Sept was found — JMA's own language is qualitative ('yaya taryō'/moderately heavy), not a measured millimeter figure.
No official casualty, injury, or building-damage reports tied to the 10-14 Sept activity were found in the sources checked.

Kyodo News' and Japan Times' own sites were not directly reachable in this session (search only surfaced aggregator/mirror coverage); their original-URL reporting for this exact window could not be independently confirmed.
